title: Durable Mission and lifecycle event contracts

scope.mission: A bounded business goal is represented as immutable tenant-scoped Mission state with server-derived organisation, project, and environment identity.
scope.agent_binding: Mission binds to immutable agent_version_id, deployment identity, and non-secret runtime configuration reference.
scope.lifecycle: MissionLifecycleEvent is append-only, versioned, causally and correlationally linked, actor-attributed, timestamped, and supports explicit terminal outcomes.
scope.authority: Caller input cannot override server-owned scope or lifecycle state; cross-tenant events are rejected.

verification.command: cd packages/atlas && npm run metadata:write && npm test && npm run build

invariants_verified: Mission creation starts at CREATED with stateVersion 1 and an initial CREATED event.
Legal transitions are explicit and terminal states reject further transitions.
New lifecycle events require current priorState, current stateVersion plus one, exact Mission ID, and exact scope.
Identical event ID/idempotency-key replay is a DUPLICATE_REPLAY and does not append twice.
Conflicting event ID/idempotency-key reuse is rejected with IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.
Mission and event objects are deep-frozen after validation/creation.
Agent source identity remains separate from deployment/runtime identity.
Public documentation manifest ships both Mission schemas.
tests_added: server-owned scope and lifecycle override rejection
immutable Agent version and deadline validation
duplicate replay and conflicting idempotency behavior
limitations: This item proves the public contract and local in-memory ledger only.
Durable database persistence, migrations, restart recovery, concurrency, CI, provider sandbox, staging, and production proof remain owned by later BMR-002 work items and are not claimed here.
No credentials, provider, paid service, package publication, or production operation was used.
verdict: ATLAS-BMR2-P1-002 = PASS — versioned Mission and append-only lifecycle event contracts are locally proven; persistence and deployment maturity remain explicitly unclaimed.
